ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a horizontal rectangle, with a vertical line segment in the middle, dividing the rectangle into two congruent squares side by side on the left and right; combined with the coordinates given in the problem, the whole rectangle is [0,2]×[0,1], and the common side is x=1. Reasoning: Let the random point be P=(x,y). For a line with slope 1/2 to pass through two unit squares, it is equivalent to the height of its intersection point at the common side x=1 falling between 0 and 1; the boundary cases have area 0 and do not affect the probability. If P is inside the left unit square, that is, 0<x<1, then when the line reaches x=1, the height is y+(1-x)/2. It requires y+(1-x)/2<1, so the bad region satisfies y>(1+x)/2. This is a right triangle above the left square, and one may take horizontal base length 1 and vertical height 1/2, with area 1/2·1·1/2=1/4. If P is inside the right unit square, that is, 1<x<2, then when the line reaches x=1, the height is y-(x-1)/2. It requires y-(x-1)/2>0, so the bad region satisfies y<(x-1)/2. This is a right triangle below the right square, likewise with base length 1 and height 1/2, area 1/4. Therefore the total bad area is 1/4+1/4=1/2. The total area of the rectangle is 2, so the desired probability is (2-1/2)/2=3/4.

method.method_draft: Use a vertical-divider crossing test. First read from the image that the 2-by-1 rectangle is split by a vertical segment into two side-by-side unit squares, so the shared boundary is the line x=1. From the text, take R=[0,2]x[0,1], P=(x,y) uniformly random, and the line slope as 1/2. A line through P passes through both unit squares exactly when it reaches the shared boundary x=1 at a height between 0 and 1. If P is in the left square, 0<x<1, the height at x=1 is y+(1-x)/2, so require y+(1-x)/2<1; the excluded region is the triangle y>(1+x)/2 in the left square, area 1/4. If P is in the right square, 1<x<2, the height at x=1 is y-(x-1)/2, so require y-(x-1)/2>0; the excluded region is the triangle y<(x-1)/2 in the right square, area 1/4. Total bad area is 1/2 out of rectangle area 2, so probability is (2-1/2)/2=3/4.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：附图显示一个横向的长方形，被中间的一条竖直线段分成左右两个并排的全等正方形；结合题目给出的坐标，这条公共边是 x=1，整个矩形是 [0,2]×[0,1]。推理：设随机点 P=(x,y)。斜率为 1/2 的直线要穿过两个单位正方形，等价于它在公共边 x=1 处的交点高度落在 0 到 1 之间。若 P 在左方单位正方形内，即 0<x<1，则直线到 x=1 时高度为 y+(1-x)/2。需要 y+(1-x)/2<1，所以坏区域满足 y>(1+x)/2。这是在左正方形右上角的三角形，底和高都为 1/2，面积为 1/4。若 P 在右方单位正方形内，即 1<x<2，则直线到 x=1 时高度为 y-(x-1)/2。需要 y-(x-1)/2>0，所以坏区域满足 y<(x-1)/2。这是在右正方形左下角的三角形，底和高都为 1/2，面积为 1/4。因此总坏面积为 1/4+1/4=1/2。矩形总面积为 2，所以所求概率为 (2-1/2)/2=3/4。

method.method_draft: Use a slope-parallel strip/intercept method. From the image, note that the only way for a slope-1/2 line to meet both side-by-side squares is for it to intersect the vertical common segment separating them. From the text, model P=(x,y) uniformly in the rectangle 0<x<2, 0<y<1. Lines of slope 1/2 have equation y=x/2+b, where b=y_P-x_P/2. The line intersects the common segment x=1, 0<y<1 exactly when 0<1/2+b<1, or -1/2<b<1/2. Thus the favorable P are those in R satisfying -1/2<y-x/2<1/2, a diagonal strip inside the 2-by-1 rectangle. The complement consists of two congruent right triangles: above y=x/2+1/2 near the upper-left corner and below y=x/2-1/2 near the lower-right corner, each with legs 1 and 1/2, area 1/4. Favorable area is 2-1/2=3/2, so the probability is (3/2)/2=3/4.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：附图显示一个水平放置的长方形，被中间一条竖直线分成左右两个相邻的全等正方形；这条竖直线就是两个单位正方形的公共边。推理：设随机点 P=(x,y) 均匀分布在长方形 R 的内部，其中 0<x<2, 0<y<1。斜率为 1/2 的直线可写成 y=x/2+b，其中 b=y_P-x_P/2。根据图中两个正方形左右相邻的结构，这条直线要同时经过两个单位正方形，等价于它与公共竖直边 x=1 在 0<y<1 的部分相交。代入 x=1，交点纵坐标为 1/2+b，所以需要 0<1/2+b<1，即 -1/2<b<1/2。因此有利点满足 -1/2<y-x/2<1/2。整个矩形面积为 2。该条带在矩形内的补集由两个直角三角形组成：左上方 y>x/2+1/2 的三角形和右下方 y<x/2-1/2 的三角形。每个三角形的直角边长分别为 1 和 1/2，面积为 (1·1/2)/2=1/4，两个共面积 1/2。因此有利面积为 2-1/2=3/2，所求概率为 (3/2)/2=3/4。

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a horizontal rectangle, with a vertical line segment in the middle, dividing the rectangle into two congruent squares side by side on the left and right; combined with the coordinates given in the problem, the whole rectangle is [0,2]×[0,1], and the common side is x=1. Reasoning: Let the random point be P=(x,y). For a line with slope 1/2 to pass through two unit squares, it is equivalent to the height of its intersection point at the common side x=1 falling between 0 and 1; the boundary cases have area 0 and do not affect the probability. If P is inside the left unit square, that is, 0<x<1, then when the line reaches x=1, the height is y+(1-x)/2. It requires y+(1-x)/2<1, so the bad region satisfies y>(1+x)/2. This is a right triangle above the left square, and one may take horizontal base length 1 and vertical height 1/2, with area 1/2·1·1/2=1/4. If P is inside the right unit square, that is, 1<x<2, then when the line reaches x=1, the height is y-(x-1)/2. It requires y-(x-1)/2>0, so the bad region satisfies y<(x-1)/2. This is a right triangle below the right square, likewise with base length 1 and height 1/2, area 1/4. Therefore the total bad area is 1/4+1/4=1/2. The total area of the rectangle is 2, so the desired probability is (2-1/2)/2=3/4.
